result:
No existing ADR/changelog convention in this repo, so here's what I'd actually push for — the diff size is irrelevant; what matters is that the *decision boundary* of an autonomous refund-approver can shift silently even when the code doesn't. A one-line PR description gives a future reviewer zero ability to tell whether that happened.

**The record should be an eval-backed decision record, not a diff description.** Contents:

1. **Why, precisely** — "cost review" plus the actual numbers (cost/latency delta) and who signed off on trading cost for a behavior change in a money-moving agent.

2. **Blast radius as of this change** — what the agent can currently do unattended (refund $ caps, tool access, any human-in-the-loop thresholds). This anchors how much scrutiny is warranted.

3. **Pre-swap baseline** — Provider A's performance on a representative eval set: correct approve/deny decisions, dollar-amount accuracy, edge cases (partial refunds, policy exceptions), and adversarial cases (prompt injection via customer-supplied text, attempts to manipulate the agent into approving out-of-policy refunds).

4. **Post-swap results on the same eval set** — Provider B run against identical cases, with a diff of *which specific cases changed outcome*, not just an aggregate pass rate. Aggregate scores can hide a new failure mode (e.g., Provider B being more persuadable by manipulated input) even while overall accuracy looks the same or better.

5. **Regressions found and disposition** — anything that changed for the worse, and whether it was fixed, mitigated, or knowingly accepted (with rationale and who accepted the risk).

6. **Guardrails status** — confirmation that caps/limits/human-review thresholds were not implicitly relying on Provider-A-specific behavior, and are unchanged or explicitly updated.

7. **Rollback plan** — how to revert, and what production signal (refund $ velocity, dispute rate, anomaly alerts) would trigger it.

8. **Post-launch monitoring** — what's being watched, for how long, by whom, after the swap goes live.

9. **Reproducibility** — link/reference to the eval harness and dataset used, so someone in six months can rerun it rather than trust a summary.

10. **Sign-off** — engineering plus whoever owns financial/customer risk for this agent (not just the PR approver).

The one-liner "swapped model per cost review" is fine as the *commit message*. What needs to exist is the linked eval report (even a short one) showing #3 and #4 actually happened before merge. If that eval doesn't exist yet, that's the real finding here — the "one-line change" framing is masking that no one has verified the new model approves/denies refunds the same way.

Want me to draft this as a template (e.g., a `CHANGES.md`/ADR entry) you can drop in and fill with your eval numbers?
